pairs.evidence: crates/contract/src/endpoints/mod.rs:30 The endpoint table is a compile-time constant catalog of the host's own HTTP routes, held in bijection with build_router. No contribution can mount a route and there is no agent runtime pipeline. A search of crates/contract/src/endpoints for plugin, subagent, mutator and assembly found nothing; `checkpoint` and `hook` appear only as dataset-freeze and webhook prose.

techniques.evidence: crates/contract/src/endpoints/mod.rs:30 All routes are host-owned compile-time constants; the API router has no contributed-router merge, so there is no mount order to defend.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/relay.rs:28 A relay task whose device died mid-run is recorded through a distinguishing prefix string in `error`, not a first-class status. Once its reclaim budget runs out it ends as `dead`, which the vocabulary defines as terminal failure. The indeterminate outcome therefore lives in prose that every consumer must re-parse, and an unknown-outcome agent action is filed as a failure.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/relay.rs:28 This is the named failure mode: a distinguishing string inside the error field, with no indeterminate value in RelayStatus. Line 47 defines Dead as 'Terminal failure — the retry budget or the device-death budget is exhausted'. Reclaim also re-runs a possibly side-effecting action, which assumes it is idempotent. The separate stale_reclaims counter is a real, partial mitigation.

crates/core/src/relay.rs:6 The service-writable tier (a cloud enqueue) can name only an action type plus parameters. Prompts and allowed tools come from the device's local, operator-held action library.
crates/core/src/relay.rs:136 A per-holder lease fence discards a late result from a superseded holder. Cancelling sits outside the leasable set, so post-cancel delivery is withheld (line 49).
